children: The offshore yuan held its gains around 6.69 per dollar on Monday, remaining at its strongest level since July 2022, as the People’s Bank of China kept its benchmark lending rates unchanged for a 16th consecutive month at record lows.
The one-year loan prime rate (LPR) was held at 3.0%, while the five-year LPR remained at 3.5%.
The decision comes as policymakers face limited room for further monetary easing as the yuan continues to strengthen and after other central banks shifted to rate hikes.
However, current conditions continue to support the possibility of a rate cut before year-end, as economic growth slows, inflation remains subdued, and credit activity stays weak.

Meanwhile, investor focus remained on high-level US-China engagement after officials from both countries met in New York on Sunday to prepare for a closely watched summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping on September 24.

title: Offshore Yuan Holds at Over 4-Year High
